parameters.content:
# 05 - AI Lead Reasoning

**What this workflow handles**
The narrow slice of the decision that genuinely needs language understanding: reading an ambiguous job title, and writing one grounded opening question a rep can actually use. Nothing else. 01 calls it as a sub-flow, and only for `tier_1`, `matched` and `needs_review` scans - competitors and out-of-scope never reach it. It hands the same lead object straight back, with the persona, tier, opening question and any guardrail warnings filled in.

**Assumptions I made**
- **An LLM should not own a tier.** Tiers move budget and rep attention; they must be reproducible and explainable. So rules decide, and the model advises.
- Most titles are not ambiguous. "Chief Information Security Officer" is a rule. "Lead Identity Infrastructure Architect" is where a model earns its place.
- A model that can invent a fact will eventually invent one in front of a customer. So every public claim must cite a URL that was supplied to it, and every quote is checked back against the real booth notes.
- Booth notes are untrusted data. If they contain instruction-like text, the model is skipped entirely and rules stand.
- Free tier means Gemini Flash, temperature 0, no tools, a bounded token budget.

**What the model may decide**
· Persona - **only** when `persona_status = ambiguous`, and only above the policy confidence floor
· Industry - only as a fallback, and only citing a supplied URL
· The opening question, why it matters now, what to listen for, one booth action
· Classification - **only** as a consequence of resolving an ambiguous persona: that resolution moves the lead from `needs_review` to `matched`, or to `tier_1` when a deterministic urgency trigger was already quoted from the booth notes. It cannot invent the urgency; the rules must have found it first.

**What it can never do**
Override a persona the rules already decided · invent urgency · clear a competitor · overturn the size or SaaS-only rules · write to the CRM · choose a Slack channel · cite a URL it was not given.

If it disagrees with a clear title rule, the disagreement is logged as a warning and **the rule wins**. `persona_source` on every record says which decided it: `rule_title_match`, `none_from_rules`, `ai_resolved_ambiguous`, `ai_found_no_persona`, `unresolved_low_confidence`. The last two are the honest failures - the model was confident there is no Oak persona, or it was not confident enough to say - and both leave the lead to a human instead of guessing.

**The flow**
1. Load the active policy and render its personas - title patterns and Oak angle - plus its target industries as the allowed industry values: change the policy, the prompt changes, no workflow edit. The headcount thresholds and disqualifiers are not rendered; the prompt only says those rules are authoritative and already applied. The confidence floor is passed as data to step 4, never asked for in the prompt.
2. Refuse outright if injection was suspected upstream.
3. Call Gemini with strict JSON output.
4. **Guard the output**: clamp every field to an allowed value, drop any URL that was not supplied, delete any urgency quote that does not appear verbatim in the booth notes, cap the score at the policy max.

`public_context` is kept on the record for audit and deliberately never printed on the card: the card's public-context line is a quoted claim with its source beside it, and a model-written sentence in that slot would break the promise that layout makes. Those sentences are only populated at all when the model cited one of the URLs it was handed.

**Where it can fail**
Unavailable, truncated, or invalid JSON - all three soft-fail to the deterministic result plus a grounded fallback question, and the card says so.

nodes.notes: Renders the active policy's personas (title patterns and Oak angle) and its target industries as the allowed industry values, so changing the policy changes the prompt with no workflow edit. The headcount thresholds and disqualifiers are not rendered; the prompt only says those rules are authoritative and already applied. The confidence floor travels as data for the guard, never as a request in the prompt.

nodes.name: Gemini Lead Analyst

options.systemMessage:
={{ $json.system_prompt + '
10. recommended_action may only ask a question, keep the person engaged, bring in the CRM owner or an Oak technical/security teammate, or capture a named missing fact. Do not invent a dashboard, demo, asset, capability, commitment, discount, meeting, or follow-up owner.
11. Never convert an allegation, unconfirmed report, policy document, hypothetical wording, or supplier terms into a factual company incident. Label uncertainty exactly or omit it.
12. A source about a similarly named company is not evidence. Use only the supplied identity-aligned source set.' }}

nodes.notes: Not trusted to judge fit - only to read a job title the rule matcher could not classify, and to write one grounded question and what to listen for. It never sees a tier, a score or a channel.

nodes.name: Guard AI Output
nodes.notes: Nothing downstream sees a raw model field: each one is clamped to an allowed value here, and any URL or urgency quote the booth notes do not support is dropped. This is also the only place an AI read moves a tier - up from needs_review when an ambiguous title is confidently resolved, down to out_of_scope when the model is confident there is no Oak persona, and nowhere at all below the policy confidence floor.
